title: GitHub Copilot — ESGCI DBA Thesis Workspace
body_md:
# GitHub Copilot — ESGCI DBA Thesis Workspace

This file is auto-loaded by GitHub Copilot on every chat request. **As of 2026-09-02, `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/` are frozen for backwards compatibility.** They remain readable and authoritative for pre-existing rules and workflows; new rules, new instructions, new skills, and new agents go under `.github/`. See Section 0.5 for the full policy.

---

## 0. Copilot-native advisor layer

Day-to-day work now runs through a GitHub Copilot custom agent, **ESGCIDBA Advisor** ([`agents/esgcidba-advisor.agent.md`](agents/esgcidba-advisor.agent.md)), set as the workspace default. It replaces Claude Code for routine drafting while inheriting `CLAUDE.md`. It authors dissertation content **directly as DOCX** (not markdown), accepts Google Drive and OneDrive paths, keeps Zotero usage unchanged, and treats the `.claude/` markdown workflow as a backup used only on explicit request.

Supporting `.github/` assets:

- Instructions: [`instructions/dba-house-style.instructions.md`](instructions/dba-house-style.instructions.md), [`instructions/docx-authoring.instructions.md`](instructions/docx-authoring.instructions.md).
- Skills: `skills/literature-review` (default), `skills/chapter-layout`, `skills/research-design-methodology`, `skills/dba-research-learning-guide`, with reusable Python utilities under `skills/_shared/scripts/`.

The pre-existing rules in `CLAUDE.md` remain authoritative for backwards compatibility; the agent and skills inherit them and never duplicate them. New rules do not go into `CLAUDE.md` — see Section 0.5.

---

## 0.5 File-freeze policy (2026-09-02)

**`CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/` are frozen.** Continue to read them and obey the rules they contain — the L1–L6 locked constraints in `CLAUDE.md`, the slash-command bodies in `.claude/commands/`, the agent personas in `.claude/agents/`, and the prompt templates in `.claude/prompts/` all remain in effect exactly as written.

**New rules, new instructions, new skills, new agents, and any newly authored discipline go under `.github/`**, never into `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/`.

| Class of asset | New location (2026-09-02 onward) | Preserved read-only location |
|---|---|---|
| Workspace-wide rule | append to this file (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`) | `CLAUDE.md` §2, §5, §7 (do not edit) |
| Rule scoped to a folder or file class | new `.github/instructions/<name>.instructions.md` with an `applyTo` glob | `CLAUDE.md` §3, §4 |
| Skill (executable domain knowledge) | `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` + `scripts/` | (no `.claude/` equivalent — skills are `.github/`-only) |
| Agent persona | `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` | `.claude/agents/<name>.md` |
| Slash-command procedure | folded into an agent or skill under `.github/` | `.claude/commands/<name>.md` |
| Prompt output template | `.github/prompts/<name>.prompt.md` | `.claude/prompts/<name>.md` |

**When a `CLAUDE.md` rule needs updating**, write a new `.github/instructions/<name>.instructions.md` that supersedes it. Name the file so the supersedence is obvious (e.g. `csv-log-discipline.instructions.md` supersedes any prior CSV rule scattered in `CLAUDE.md`). Never edit `CLAUDE.md` itself.

**When an existing `.claude/` file needs a behavioural change**, write a superseding file under `.github/` (typically a new skill or instruction file) that takes precedence for future runs. Leave the `.claude/` original untouched so historical sessions remain reproducible.

This policy itself is now the rule for governing rules. If the user asks for a new convention, style guide, integrity check, or discipline, always pick the smallest applicable `.github/` target from the table above and never touch `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/`.

---

## 1. Source of truth — read first, obey always

On the **first turn of every session** (and any time the user changes topic), open and read [`../CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) in full. It defines:

- Locked constraints **L1–L6** (quantitative methodology; free public secondary data only; evaluation research + quasi-experimental identification; positivist / post-positivist + hypothetico-deductive paradigm; solo execution; APA 7).
- The folder map (`V2/` is active; `V1_AI_Notebooks/` is legacy — never modify).
- House style (critical not sycophantic; theory-anchored; APA 7; British English; no emojis; clarity over complexity; no LaTeX in proposals; no AI-tooling tells).
- Vocabulary discipline (positivist terms only).
- ESGCI assignment pipeline (A01–A06) and current state.
- Anti-patterns to refuse (maturity models, surveys, interviews, paid datasets, mixed-methods/interpretivist framings).

These instructions **override any default Copilot behaviour** and apply to every response in this workspace.

---

## 2. Slash commands — `.claude/commands/<name>.md`

When the user types `/<name>` in chat, locate `.claude/commands/<name>.md`, read it, and **execute its body as the prompt for this turn**. The YAML frontmatter (`description`, `argument-hint`, `tools`, `model`) describes invocation; the markdown body is the procedure to follow. Do not paraphrase or shortcut the body — follow it step by step.

Quick routing reference (full library is the contents of `.claude/commands/`):

| Family | Examples |
|---|---|
| A02 literature-review section drafting | `/draft-lr-s1` … `/draft-lr-s12`, `/draft-lr-all`, `/integrate-lr`, `/check-lr-section`, `/status-lr` |
| LR diagrams | `/lr-s2-diagram`, `/lr-s4-diagram`, `/lr-s5-diagram`, `/lr-s6-diagram` |
| Reading & triage (T1–T4) | `/deep-read`, `/targeted-read`, `/t2-batch`, `/abstract-triage`, `/refs-only`, `/triage-rr-csv`, `/triage-consensus`, `/triage-acm-bib` |
| Synthesis & analysis | `/lit-summarise`, `/meta-analyse`, `/find-gap`, `/audit-lr-refs`, `/audit-paradigm`, `/check-lr-plagiarism` |
| Proposal development | `/draft-a01`, `/develop-keywords`, `/refine-rq`, `/scrutinize-topic`, `/check-causal`, `/eli5`, `/formalize` |
| Quality & compliance | `/no-ai-tells`, `/viva-prep` |
| Utilities | `/commit-push`, `/journal-from-commits`, `/md-to-docx` |

If a command name is ambiguous or unmatched, list the closest matches from `.claude/commands/` and ask the user to disambiguate — do not guess.

---

## 3. Agents — `.claude/agents/<name>.md`

When a task matches an agent's domain (per the agent's frontmatter `description`), **adopt the role defined in that file** for the duration of the task. Use it as a persona / specialised system prompt overlay; do not call the Claude Code `Agent` tool (GHCP has no equivalent).

Routing table (verbatim descriptions from `.claude/agents/<file>` frontmatter):

| Agent | Use it when… |
|---|---|
| `apa-formatter` | Format, audit, fix, or generate APA 7 in-text citations and reference lists. Flags fabricated, duplicated, or unverifiable references. |
| `critical-examiner` | Stress-test a topic, RQ, design, draft chapter, or full A0x submission before the candidate hands it in. Generates ranked viva questions with counter-positions. |
| `data-source-scout` | Find, verify, and document free public secondary data sources for a given research question. Returns a data inventory. |
| `deep-read-orchestrator` | Orchestrate a deep-read of a single academic paper. Spawns `lit-chunk-reader` sub-tasks for page ranges, then synthesises. |
| `lit-chunk-reader` | Subordinate to `lit-summarise-ref` / `deep-read-orchestrator`. Reads a PDF page range and returns a 200–400 word section summary. |
| `lit-summarise-ref` | Per-reference summariser. Reads one Zotero item (abstract + PDF/HTML), produces a structured summary with proposal-alignment critique and percentage scores. |
| `literature-reviewer` | Systematic literature-review helper. Theme-organised synthesis with APA 7 citations and gap identification. Never invents references. |
| `meta-analyst` | Synthesise all literature summaries into a meta-analysis report with hypothesis-support mapping, scope-reduction recommendations, and a revised proposal draft. |
| `methodologist` | Quasi-experimental design critic (DiD, synthetic control, RDD, event study, CausalImpact). Adversarial by default. |
| `plagiarism-checker` | Internal-corpus plagiarism scanner for A02 LR sections. Deterministic n-gram overlap against the closed A02 corpus. |
| `proposal-translator` | Bidirectional translation between formal academic prose and plain-language ELI5 (used by `/eli5` and `/formalize`). |
| `rr-triage-rater` | Rates a single Research Rabbit CSV row against the v10 proposal scope. Abstract-only — does not read PDFs. |

If multiple agents could apply, prefer the most specific one. If none match cleanly, proceed in the default voice but still obey CLAUDE.md house style.

---

## 4. Prompt templates — `.claude/prompts/<name>.md`

Files in `.claude/prompts/` are **output-format templates** referenced by specific commands (e.g. `/triage-rr-csv` writes against `rr-triage-template.md`). Load them only when the invoking command's body instructs you to. Do not produce free-form output when a template exists for the task.

---

## 5. Authoring new agents, commands, or prompts

**As of 2026-09-02**, new authoring goes into `.github/` counterpart folders, not `.claude/`. The `.claude/` scaffold is preserved read-only for backwards compatibility (Section 0.5).

| New asset | Destination | Convention |
|---|---|---|
| Instruction file (rules, discipline, style, integrity checks) | `.github/instructions/<name>.instructions.md` | YAML frontmatter: `description`, `applyTo` glob. Body = rules. |
| Skill (executable domain knowledge, scripts, procedure) | `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` + `.github/skills/<name>/scripts/` | Frontmatter: `description`. Body = when-to-use, procedure, history. |
| Agent persona | `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` | Frontmatter: `name`, `description`, `tools` (optional), `model` (optional). Body = role. |
| Prompt output template | `.github/prompts/<name>.prompt.md` | Frontmatter minimal. Body = template shape. |

Before drafting, open one or two existing files in the target `.github/` subfolder (for example `.github/instructions/dba-house-style.instructions.md` or a nearby SKILL.md) and mirror their frontmatter shape and section structure. The conventions in CLAUDE.md §5 (APA 7, British English, no emojis, no AI-tells, verifiable references, theory-anchored, free public data only) still apply and must be enforced.

**Never create new material under `.claude/`.** If a legacy `.claude/` file needs a behavioural change, write a superseding file under `.github/` (typically a new instruction file or skill) that takes precedence for future runs. Leave the `.claude/` original untouched so historical sessions remain reproducible.

---

## 6. Amending workspace rules

**`CLAUDE.md` is frozen (Section 0.5).** Do not edit it. The L1–L6 locked constraints, the folder map, and the house-style rules in `CLAUDE.md` remain authoritative and readable, but no new rules are added to it.

When the user introduces, refines, or revokes a rule (workspace convention, house style, discipline, applies-to pattern, integrity rule, log-schema requirement, and so on), pick the smallest applicable `.github/` target from the table below.

| Class of amendment | Target |
|---|---|
| New workspace-wide rule (applies to every response) | append to this file (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`) |
| New rule tied to a folder, file class, or artefact type | new `.github/instructions/<name>.instructions.md` with an `applyTo` glob |
| New rule specific to one skill's behaviour | update that skill's `.github/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` and, if procedural, its `scripts/` |
| New rule superseding an existing `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/` rule | new `.github/instructions/<name>.instructions.md`; do not edit the legacy file |
| State change (active assignment, current artefact version, deadline) | update `.github/copilot-instructions.md` §9 or add a state note to the relevant SKILL.md; do not edit `CLAUDE.md` §8 |

### Edit procedure

1. Identify the smallest applicable target from the table above.
2. If the target already exists, edit it in the same prose, table, or list style as its surrounding content. Match British English, APA 7, no emojis, no AI-tells.
3. If creating a new instruction file, use a YAML frontmatter with `description` and (usually) an `applyTo` glob so Copilot surfaces the rule only in relevant contexts.
4. Before saving, **state the diff to the user in one sentence** (for example, "Adding a new `.github/instructions/csv-log-discipline.instructions.md` that requires every PRISMA log to carry a `stable_id` column. Source: 2026-09-02 review."). Save only on confirmation.
5. If the amendment relates to L1–L6 (the locked constraints in `CLAUDE.md`) or house style, state explicitly that the legacy rule in `CLAUDE.md` remains in force and that the new `.github/` file layers on top of it or supersedes it. Do not touch `CLAUDE.md`.

If the user phrases a change as "from now on…", "always…", "never…", "by default…", "as a rule…", or "going forward…", treat it as a candidate rule and follow the table above.

---

## 7. Project defaults (mirrored from `.claude/settings.json`)

GHCP has no environment-variable mechanism, so the equivalents are reproduced here as plain rules. Apply to every output unless the user explicitly overrides:

- **Citation style:** APA 7.
- **Writing locale:** British English (en-GB). Never mix with American English.
- **Paradigm:** positivist / post-positivist, hypothetico-deductive. Reject interpretivist or abductive framings unless the user explicitly pivots.
- **Data policy:** free and publicly accessible secondary data only. Refuse Lightcast, Revelio, SDC, Compustat, MSCI ESG, or any paid licence.
- **Project domain:** ESGCI-DBA-Thesis (applied research dissertation).

---

## 8. Safety prohibitions (mirrored deny-list)

Refuse the following without explicit, in-message user authorisation, and warn the user about the consequences before complying even when authorised:

- `rm -rf` or equivalent recursive deletion.
- `git push --force` (and `--force-with-lease` on shared branches).
- `git reset --hard` against shared history.
- Any operation that overwrites uncommitted work, drops a database, rewrites published commits, or skips git hooks (`--no-verify`).

For ordinary git operations (`git status`, `git diff`, `git log`, `ls`, `cat`, file reads, web fetches), proceed without asking.

---

## 9. Reminders for the GHCP harness

- The active workstream is `V2/`. Treat `V1_AI_Notebooks/` as a museum.
- Never overwrite a prior version of an artefact — create `..._vN+1.md`.
- Use the project virtual environment for Python: `.venv/Scripts/python` on Windows, `.venv/bin/python` on Unix. Never use the system Python.
- The current assignment focus, locked theory, canonical proposal version, and latest artefacts are tracked in `CLAUDE.md` §8 — re-read it if uncertain.
- When in doubt about scope, paradigm, or data feasibility, **ask before drafting** rather than producing something that will need to be discarded.
